The presidential election in Wisconsin is now, officially, over.
Ten Republicans on Tuesday cast the state’s 10 electoral college votes for President-elect Donald Trump, and Vice President-elect JD Vance.
Trump won Wisconsin by about 30,000 votes in November.
He lost the state in 2020 by about 22,000 votes.
Former Wisconsin Gov.
Tommy Thompson said that has become a hallmark of Wisconsin: razor thing election margins.
Republicans voted on Tuesday after going to court to push back the electoral vote because of a difference between state and federal laws.
Wisconsin’s vote on Tuesday took less than 10 minutes.
It took another 10 for the electors to sign-off on the official paperwork.
The vote this year was different from the last presidential electoral vote in Wisconsin.
In 2020, Republicans voted for an alternate slate of electors as part of a “just in case” strategy to re-elect President Trump.
That vote is now at the center of a long-running criminal investigation from Attorney General Josh Kaul.
